slides.title: A Congress Is an Operation, Not an Event
bullets: An MSL does not simply attend a congress
It is a medical operation with objectives set in advance
Success is measured in results, not hours of presence
The non-negotiable question: what do we want to achieve, and how will we know?

slides.title: Every Congress Objective Fits One of Four Buckets
bullets: Scientific intelligence: new data, emerging KOL thinking, rising research questions
Relationship: strengthen or start priority KOL and DOL relationships
Insight generation: systematically capture what the community thinks and needs
Non-promotional dissemination: get company evidence to the right audience with context

slides.title: Objectives Set First Change How You Plan
bullets: Lets you rank must-attend sessions against merely interesting ones
Clarifies which KOLs need a formal meeting versus a hallway chat
Sets the insight questions to explore actively in every conversation
Replaces passively waiting for whatever comes up

slides.title: Objectives Must Align With the Bigger Plan
bullets: Not a solo MSL initiative: tied to the product's global medical plan
Also tied to the team's annual congress plan and evidence plan
A pre-launch congress focuses on awareness and unmet-need insights
A mature-product congress focuses on real-world data and residual evidence gaps

slides.title: Every Objective Needs a Verifiable Indicator
bullets: Number of qualified interactions with priority KOLs
Number of quality insights captured and documented
Coverage of key scientific sessions
New connections started with potential research collaborators
Without indicators, evaluation is just a subjective impression

takeaway.title: A congress delivers medical value only when its objectives are defined before it starts
bullets: Objectives fall into intelligence, relationship, insight, and dissemination goals
They must connect to the product's medical plan, not stand alone
Verifiable indicators are what turn attendance into a measurable return
